meta.name: Analyze weekly KPI drops with Google Sheets, Gmail, and GPT-4o-mini

name: Monitor your services and email you when one goes down

nodes.name: Every Monday at 9am
nodes.notes:
Runs every Monday at 9AM automatically.

Change the schedule if needed:
- Every day at 9AM: 0 9 * * *
- Every weekday: 0 9 * * 1-5
- Twice a week: 0 9 * * 1,4

For daily monitoring, also reduce dropThreshold in Set Config Values to around 10.
No credentials needed.

nodes.name: Set config
nodes.notes:
REPLACE THESE 5 VALUES:

1. sheetId
   Open your Google Sheet in browser
   URL: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ABC123/edit
   Copy the part between /d/ and /edit

   Create a tab called: KPI Log
   Row 1 headers (example — use your own metrics):
   Week | Leads | Revenue | Sessions | Conversions | Conv Rate

   Each Monday before 9AM, add one new row with that week's numbers.
   Example row: 21 Apr 2026 | 142 | 28400 | 8920 | 67 | 4.7

2. alertEmail
   Who receives the anomaly alert
   Example: you@example.com

3. senderName
   Your name for email sign-offs
   Example: Rahul Dutt

4. dropThreshold
   Percentage drop that triggers an alert
   Default: 20 means any metric that falls 20% or more sends an alert
   Set to 15 for more sensitive alerts
   Set to 30 if you only want alerts for serious drops

5. businessContext
   One line about your business — GPT uses this for relevant analysis
   Example: SEO agency serving law firms and medical practices
   Example: E-commerce store selling health supplements
   Example: B2B SaaS for project management

nodes.name: Read the KPI log
nodes.notes:
Reads all rows from the KPI Log tab.

How to connect:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and enable the Google Sheets API
2. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Google Sheets OAuth2
3. Authenticate and connect to this node

The workflow uses the two most recent rows for comparison.
The very first run needs at least 2 rows to function.
Add more metrics by adding more columns — the workflow detects them automatically.

nodes.name: Compare the last two weeks
nodes.notes:
Compares the two most recent rows from the KPI Log.

For every numeric metric column it calculates:
- Current value vs previous value
- Percentage change
- Whether the drop exceeds the threshold

Anomalies are sorted by severity — worst drop first.
Non-numeric columns and zero-value previous weeks are skipped safely.

The workflow auto-detects all metric columns except Week and Date.
Add any metric to the sheet and it will be tracked automatically.

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Anything dropped?
nodes.notes:
TRUE — one or more metrics dropped beyond the threshold — run AI analysis and send alert
FALSE — all metrics are healthy or within normal range — end silently

No email is sent when everything is healthy.
This keeps the alert meaningful — when you do get an email, it matters.

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Explain the drops
nodes.notes:
GPT analyzes the KPI anomalies and returns 5 structured fields:

1. executiveSummary — 2-3 sentences on overall week performance
2. anomalyAnalysis — per-metric breakdown with likely causes and immediate actions
3. positiveHighlights — any metrics that improved
4. weeklyOutlook — what these drops mean for the next 30 days
5. priorityAction — the one thing to fix this week

The businessContext from config makes the analysis relevant to your industry.
Output is in $json.output

parameters.text:
=You are a business analytics expert specializing in KPI analysis and {{ $json.businessContext }}.

Weekly KPI comparison:
Current week: {{ $json.currentWeekLabel }}
Previous week: {{ $json.previousWeekLabel }}

All metric changes this week:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.allChanges, null, 2) }}

Metrics that dropped significantly (more than {{ $json.dropThreshold }}%):
{{ JSON.stringify($json.anomalies, null, 2) }}

Analyze these results and return ONLY a valid JSON object. No extra text. No markdown. No backticks.

Required fields:

executiveSummary
2 to 3 sentences summarizing overall performance this week. Reference the actual numbers. Be direct and specific.

anomalyAnalysis
Array of objects — one per anomaly in the anomalies list. Each object must have exactly:
metric: the exact metric name as given
likelyCauses: array of exactly 2 to 3 specific possible reasons this metric dropped. Relate each reason to the business context and the specific metric.
immediateActions: array of exactly 2 to 3 concrete, specific steps to investigate and address this drop within the next 48 hours.

positiveHighlights
Array of up to 3 strings. Any metrics that performed well this week worth noting. If nothing improved, return an empty array.

weeklyOutlook
One sentence. What these drops could mean for the business over the next 30 days if not addressed.

priorityAction
One sentence. The single most important thing to investigate or fix this week. Be specific — name the metric and the action.

nodes.name: Chat model
nodes.notes:
Connect your OpenAI API credential here.

1. Go to platform.openai.com/api-keys
2. Create a new key
3. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → OpenAI API
4. Connect to this node

Model: gpt-4o-mini
temperature: 0.3 for consistent, analytical output
Cost: about $0.003 per weekly alert

nodes.name: Output Parser - Analysis
nodes.notes:
Schema: 5 required fields.
Ensures GPT always returns clean consistent data.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Build the alert email
nodes.notes:
Builds the full alert email from GPT output.

Email has 6 sections:
1. Executive summary
2. All metrics table with this week vs last week
3. Per-metric anomaly analysis with causes and actions
4. Positive highlights
5. Weekly outlook
6. Priority action

Subject line includes the worst-performing metrics and their drop percentages.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Send the alert
nodes.notes:
Sends the KPI anomaly alert to your email.

How to connect:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and enable the Gmail API
2. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Gmail OAuth2
3. Authenticate and connect to this node

This email only fires when at least one metric dropped beyond the threshold.
Healthy weeks produce no email — no noise.

To also send to Slack or Telegram, add those nodes in parallel
and connect them from Build Alert Email alongside this node.

nodes.name: All healthy, no email
nodes.notes:
FALSE branch — no metrics dropped beyond the threshold.
All metrics are within normal range this week.
No email is sent — no noise in your inbox.
Result logged in the execution history.
No changes needed.

assignments.name: result
assignments.value: =All KPIs healthy this week. No metric dropped more than {{ $json.dropThreshold }}%. {{ $json.totalMetrics }} metrics checked. No email sent.

parameters.content:
## 1. Read the numbers
One config node holds your sheet, alert email, drop threshold and business type. The KPI Log tab is read every Monday morning.

## 2. Compare and flag
The last two rows are compared column by column. Every metric except Week is detected automatically, so adding a column needs no changes here.

## 3. Explain and alert
If something dropped past your threshold, GPT writes the likely causes and the actions to take, and you get one email. A healthy week sends nothing.

# Weekly KPI anomaly detector with AI explanations

Every business tracks weekly numbers, and most teams notice a sharp drop days after it happened. This reads your KPI sheet every Monday, compares this week with last week, and emails you only when something falls past your threshold, with an AI written explanation of the likely causes and what to do about it.

### How it works
1. A Monday schedule fires and one config node holds your sheet, alert email, drop threshold and a line about your business.
2. The KPI Log tab is read and the two most recent rows are compared.
3. A Code node works out the percentage change for every metric column and flags anything that dropped past your threshold, twenty percent by default. Metric columns are detected automatically, so adding a column needs no changes.
4. If nothing dropped, the run ends quietly and no email is sent.
5. If something did, GPT reads the drops alongside your business context and writes a plain language summary, the likely causes, and specific actions to take this week.
6. That analysis is built into one email and sent to you.

### Setup
1. Add your OpenAI API key and connect your Google Sheets and Gmail accounts.
2. Create a tab called KPI Log with a Week column followed by one column per metric, for example Leads, Revenue, Sessions, Conversions.
3. Each Monday, paste that week's numbers into a new row. Two rows are needed before the first comparison can run.
4. Open Set config and replace the sheet ID, alert email, your name and your business type.

### Customization
Lower dropThreshold to catch smaller dips, or switch the schedule to daily and use a Date column instead of Week.
